title: Six new stalls on the Row this season
summary: Hand-pulled noodles, wood-fired pita, and a woman who sharpens your knives while you shop.
content:
Every winter we read through the stall applications at somebody's kitchen table, and every winter it gets harder to say no. This year six new vendors made it onto the Row.

You'll find hand-pulled noodles at the north end, wood-fired pita next to the band, and Ruth's knife sharpening by the crosswalk. Drop your kitchen knives off when you arrive and pick them up on your way home. There's also a new potter, a hot sauce maker and a fifteen-year-old who bakes better rye than any of us.

The noodles come from Mei and Tom Lin, who have been pulling dough at markets two towns over for six years. Get there before 7, or get in line.

Anders Holm is the potter. You've probably drunk from one of his mugs already, because half the Row uses them. The hot sauce is from the Brennan sisters, who are entering the Throwdown in August. Their mild is not mild.

And the rye is Priya's. She's fifteen, she started baking during a snow week, and she usually sells out by 8.

Come say hello. They're all a little nervous, and all of them could use a regular.
